title: Ostia (Confessions 9)
hook: Augustine and Monica, at a window, talk of heaven; days later she dies

segments.voice: Yesterday, Augustine and the stolen pears. Your line was know why you do it.

Two people are leaning at a window that looks out on a garden. The house is in Ostia, the port of Rome. They're resting after a long journey overland, waiting for a ship to carry them home to Africa. One is Augustine, newly baptized. The other is his mother, Monica, who wept and prayed over him through all his wandering. Nobody else is in the room. And they begin to talk, quietly, about what the life of the saints with God might be like.

Augustine tells it in the ninth book of his Confessions. Their talk climbs, step by step: past every pleasure of the body, past the beauty of earth and sky, sun and moon and stars, past even their own minds, reaching toward the Wisdom by which all things are made. And for a moment, he writes, they touched it, just barely, with the whole force of the heart. Then they sighed, and came back down to the sound of their own voices, to words that have a beginning and an end. He wonders what it would be like if that moment simply went on, and reaches for Jesus's words in Matthew's Gospel, in the King James: "enter thou into the joy of thy lord." Then Monica speaks. Son, she says, nothing in this life delights me anymore. What am I still doing here? There was one thing I wanted to stay for: to see you a Christian before I died. God has given me that, and more. Days later, she falls ill with a fever. Near the end, one of her sons wishes she could die in her own country, not in a strange place. She waves it away. Lay this body anywhere, she says. Only remember me at the altar of the Lord, wherever you are. Augustine holds back his tears at her burial, and later, alone, lets them come. Notice where this reaching for God happens. Not in a desert, not in a church. At a window, in a borrowed house, between a mother and a son who had been far apart and found their way back, just talking about what mattered.

Picture someone you love beside you at a window, with nowhere to be: a parent, a child, a friend, a partner. Find one question you'd want to ask them, about what they hope for, what they're grateful for, or what they think happens at the end, and hear yourself asking it gently. If you pray, hold them before God; if you don't, hold them in your attention.
Ostia. The port where Augustine and Monica, at a window, reached for God together, days before she died.
Your line: at the window. A borrowed house, a quiet talk, and a moment of reaching for God. Day seven hundred eighty.

howItsDone: Catholic, Orthodox and Anglican Christians remember Monica as a saint, often as a patron of mothers who pray for their children; the scene at Ostia is read as part of Augustine's Confessions.

chat.says: Where did Augustine and his mother share that famous moment of reaching for God?
options: At a window in Ostia, just talking, while they waited for a ship home.
In a desert cave, after months of fasting and silence side by side.
At the altar in Milan, on the very day Augustine was baptized.
chat.meaning: It happened at a window in a borrowed house at Ostia, waiting to sail home: not in a desert, not in a church.

Monica.meaning: Augustine's mother, who prayed for him through his wandering

Confessions.meaning: Augustine's book telling his life to God, as a long prayer

Wisdom.meaning: here, God's wisdom, through which all things are made

sources.quoted: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.

notes: Confessions 9.10.23–26: window over the garden, house at Ostia, rest after the journey before the voyage, the ascent, 'touched it a little', return to words with beginning and end, 'Enter into the joy of thy Lord'. Paraphrased; confirm.
Monica's words (9.10.26) and burial request (9.11.27) paraphrased. The text says the fever came within about five days; the script says only 'days later' (index wording).
Augustine restrained tears at the burial and wept later alone (9.12.29–33). Confirm.
'Monica, who wept and prayed over him through all his wandering' draws on Confessions 3.11.19 and elsewhere; confirm.
howItsDone: churches that keep a feast for Monica and 'patron of mothers'; confirm. Praying for the dead is not discussed, to avoid stating church differences without a source.
Editor: removed the superlative 'the book's great moment'; 'had hurt each other' changed to 'had been far apart', since the text does not say Monica hurt him.
Audit: Confessions 9.11.27 has one son (Navigius, not named) wishing she might die in her own land, not 'her sons' planning to take her body home; voice and fork setup corrected.
